sections.kicker: Prepared for Marmelade by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your site and your Instagram the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: Marmelade owns a clear idea on Instagram. The site opens with rugs.
sections.keep: Your customers' words: "I love every little detail in the prayer garment!" Detail is already what people notice.

sections.label: Front door
title: Three things people
meet first.
Three things
people meet
first.

pins.quote: What you wear for prayer, made special.
pins.what: Your bio has the whole brand in one line.
pins.why: Prayer wear made special is why Marmelade and not the next abaya shop. The site never says it.
pins.how: Make this the first line on the site.
pins.label: Your bio
pins.cost: Site visitors meet a store, not the idea 135K people followed.

pins.what: The first thing the site says is about rugs.
pins.why: Leading with a side line blurs what Marmelade is, which is part of what feels off.
pins.how: Open with prayer wear and give rugs their own place.
pins.label: Your site
pins.cost: New visitors leave unsure what you make.

pins.quote: I love every little detail in the prayer garment!
pins.what: Customers praise the details, the scent and the softness.
pins.why: Those details are a visual language waiting to be used.
pins.how: Show the stitches, the folds and the scent in your photos and words.
pins.label: Your reviews
pins.cost: The thing people love most stays in the reviews.

sections.intro: You said something feels off and you want to look like the brand you are. Here is where the gap shows.
